cards.note: External plugin is a self-contained npm bundle: dsh.bundle.patch -> cordis.patch.yml insert row, dsh.client web half, no repository-plugin artifacts.
The manifest declares only dsh.client; no legacy dshClient field or dsh.plugin.json exists in source or in the packed tarball.
dsh.client (platform web) is declared in the source and packed manifest, so client-modules scans the package and the client bundle joins the boot graph.
Every consumed client service (slots, locale, sessions, conversation) is declared in the client inject array; no undeclared ctx.get or property access remains.
No optional host service is probed; the only optional read is a missing slot prop (useChat), which is not a Cordis service.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and decodes no session event fields.
Not a self-rendering client: entries mount into the official shell, and at alpha.2 the client ctx.sessions service exists and is the official current-session scope source.
No task/job output tailing; history comes from the chat snapshot and the local draft store.
No host-side services, HTTP routes, or task-event listeners are used (client-only plugin).
Image attachment references are never read or persisted; the text-block filter skips image blocks.
The plugin does not register, wrap, parse, or snapshot read_image.
No DeepSeek LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment upload cache.
No APIProxy and no ctx.remote use; the client half reaches domain services directly.
Target is alpha.2 (A2-01 restores ignorable); the plugin writes no persisted session events either way.
No host-source patches and no imports from internal session-view paths; reads use public snapshots.
Ships a bundle patch but reads no profile files and hardcodes no DSH_HOME; the profile owns the composition.
No headless wrapper or process-output parsing in the repository.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset, or dispatch-waterfall types are used.
No permission/approval policy, WebFetch handling, or audit hooks.
The plugin serves no custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route and no /api path; the web probe used the official token->Cookie flow unchanged.
No model-provider plugin and no settings page.
Registers an empty namespace in the shipped zh/en locales through the public ctx.locale.register; adds no language and carries no i18n patch.
No subagent orchestration or provider/model selection.
Informational deployment/privacy notice about the official DeepSeek adapter; no plugin code path.
No PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workarounds exist in the plugin.
No session-log upload code; that is a deployment opt-in.
The repository ships no browser acceptance script or wrapper; the migration used the documented token->Cookie + __DSH_BOOT__ procedure as a manual check.
No structured-question answerer registration.
No agent-preset resolution or preset roots.
No @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/message import and no TPS computation.
The bundle patch only inserts this plugin row; it never restates dsh-base rows such as session-telemetry-otel.
Does not import @earendil-works/pi-ai or any provider/auth package.
No dsh-client-runtime import or inject edge remains; dsh.client.inject and peers list only real client rows, and react comes from the platform seed table.

The client bundle registers __ModuleLoader__.load id @bench/dsh-bench-history-dock; package.json name and the insert row carry the same identity (verified in the alpha.2 boot graph and combo-route bundle).

Session content is read through the same-slot official useChat standard prop (ChatSnapshot.order + nodes.get()), alpha.2 keyed replacement for session.nodes; the SessionBinding event window stays the non-React alternative.

The composer is located as the [data-composer-input] contenteditable inside [data-composer-card] with a contenteditable=false guard, the caret gate uses the Range API, and the draft write goes through SessionInput.setDraft.
No MarkdownText / fenced CodeBlock rendering from ui-primitives.
ctx.connection.api is not consumed; no history/transcript RPC calls.
No subagent descriptors are built or asserted.
No workspace navigation or directory-picker calls.
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents.
No ctx.remote unary calls or Remote failure handling.
Peers sit on the exact ^0.1.2-alpha.2 cohort (cordis ^4.0.2), the removed dsh-client-runtime peer is gone, and pack contents are an explicit allowlist (verified with npm pack).
No startup wrapper or CI matrix in the repository; the real-host probe ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the failing window.
pluginInventory/list is not consumed or validated.
No host facts are read; the client uses local services only.
The plugin mounts no tool/agent packages and installs through the shipped bundle, which already mounts session-projection.
ctx.settings.register/update/get is not used; the plugin has no settings namespace.
